title: What bands played when he started: songs and blues
summary: Early bands played songs like Japanese Sandman and blues such as How Come You Do Me Like You Do, St. Louis, Memphis and Beale Street Blues.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Where the blues came from: Handy, Bolden and early blues

blocks.x: But when you first started playing with bands, they weren't playing Dixieland -- they weren't playing Ragtime -- they were --
They were not either one and --
What were they playing? Did you call it anything?
Let me think if I can think of anything -- of any songs. I'm trying to think of (inaudible).
That was one of the songs we used to play. That don't sound like Dixieland does it?
No. Well, it's a song -- so is it playing songs or is --
Yeah, playing songs yeah, around they town. They was playing songs and the blues -- you know -- and things like that.

When you say blues, would be playing the blues in the sense that you could say to the band if you were calling the tunes -- say let's play the blues in B flat. Could you do that then, or was the blues like a specific piece that was based on the blues.
Well, some of them was and some of them was just plain blues. Some of them was taken like "How Come You Do Me Like You Do"? Now that was -- that's a sort of a blues --
You know. They got it -- the stop
sign (singing). That was -- I think that was around the time I came along and they had the St. Louis Blues, and the Memphis Blues, and Beale Street Blues. They were distinctly the blues.
Did you mean the blues as a different blues than the others?
All right. That's really almost like a song --
Yes. It's a song as it is. And --
